comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C14-C17. Both evaluations support that somatic DDR functions are normal in the Topbp1B5/B5 model, with OpenEval citing specific experimental data (clonogenic assays, western blots, immunofluorescence) and peer reviewers accepting this as part of the separation-of-function characterization.

Perfect agreement on claims C24-C25. Both evaluations support the MLH1/MLH3 imbalance findings. OpenEval notes the functional significance cannot be determined without diplotene cells, while peer reviewers do not challenge these crossover marker findings as part of the comprehensive characterization.

Perfect agreement on claims C32-C33. Both evaluations support the reduced CHK1 phosphorylation finding. OpenEval notes C33 is an inference based on published data, while Reviewer 1 explicitly mentions CHK phosphorylation defects and accepts the interpretation that it is not causal.

Perfect agreement on claims C39-C41. Both evaluations strongly support that sex body formation and chromatin modifications are intact despite silencing defects. This is recognized by all peer reviewers as a key distinguishing feature of the model.

Agreement on claims C49-C51 with some uncertainty. OpenEval supports the detailed temporal analysis of MSCI dynamics, but Reviewer 1 specifically questions whether alternative hypotheses about MSCI initiation versus maintenance are possible, suggesting the interpretation may not be definitive.

Perfect agreement on claims C52-C54. Both evaluations strongly support that this represents a unique model separating MSCI from other meiotic functions. All peer reviewers recognize this as the key conceptual advance and main strength of the study.

Strong agreement on claims C18-C19, with peer result also covering C59. Both evaluations support the biochemical characterization of the B5 mutation and reduced ATR-TOPBP1 interaction. OpenEval notes uncertainty about exact mechanisms, while peer reviewers accept the molecular characterization without challenge.

Perfect agreement on claims C27-C28. Both evaluations support the subtle synapsis defect findings. OpenEval questions the biological significance relative to the severe phenotype, while peer reviewers accept it as a minor defect consistent with the overall phenotype.

Strong agreement on claims C4-C8, with peer result also covering C9-C11. Both evaluations support the core phenotypic characterization of the Topbp1B5/B5 model including viability, fertility defects, and meiotic arrest. All peer reviewers affirm these findings as solid.

Strong agreement on claims C29-C31, with peer result also covering C20-C21. Both evaluations support that DDR protein recruitment and canonical ATR signaling are intact. Peer reviewers accept this as evidence for separation of MSCI from other meiotic functions.

Strong agreement on claims C42-C45, with peer result also covering C46-C48. Both evaluations strongly support the scRNAseq evidence for MSCI defects. Peer reviewers emphasize the quality and care of the transcriptomic work, with the Editor stating the evidence is solid.

Strong agreement on claims C34-C35, with peer result also covering C37-C38. Both evaluations support the phosphoproteomic identification of SETX as a specific defect. Multiple peer reviewers explicitly affirm the reduced SETX phosphorylation and localization findings.

Agreement on claims C46-C48 regarding MSCI defect confirmation. OpenEval supports these claims based on scRNAseq comparison to published mutants, while peer result R9 covers these claims as part of broader transcriptomic evidence (C42-C48) that reviewers find convincing.

Strong agreement on claims C12-C13, with peer result also covering C22-C23, C26. Both evaluations support this as a key distinction from prior work showing normal synapsis completion and H1t expression despite MSCI defects. Peer reviewers explicitly recognize this separation as a distinguishing feature.

Agreement on claims C9-C11 regarding meiotic arrest at pachynema. OpenEval supports these claims with histological and cytological data, while peer result R1 covers these as part of the broader core phenotype (C4-C11) that all reviewers affirm.

Partial agreement on claims C20-C23. OpenEval supports normal progression through early prophase I including synapsis and DSB repair. Peer result R2 covers C22-C23 and C26 as part of recognizing normal sex body formation as a key distinguishing feature.

Partial agreement on claims C20-C21. OpenEval supports normal early prophase I progression, while peer result R5 covers these claims as part of broader acceptance (C20-C21, C29-C31) of normal meiotic functions separate from MSCI defects.

Agreement on claim C38 regarding SETX localization defect. OpenEval supports this with immunofluorescence including 3D-SIM data, while peer result R7 covers this as part of broader SETX findings (C34-C35, C37-C38) that multiple reviewers explicitly affirm.

Agreement on claim C59 regarding B5 mutation molecular basis. OpenEval supports this with experimental data and citations, while peer result R4 covers this as part of accepting the biochemical characterization (C18-C19, C59) of the B5 mutation.

Agreement on claim C37 regarding SETX context. OpenEval supports this with citations establishing SETX's role, while peer result R7 covers this as part of the broader SETX findings (C34-C35, C37-C38) that reviewers accept.

OpenEval supports claims C1-C3 regarding baseline phenotypes from prior Topbp1 loss studies with citations to published work. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses these background/context claims.

OpenEval supports claims C55-C57 establishing the separation-of-function nature of the B5 allele with citations and MEF data. While peer reviewers accept the overall separation-of-function concept, no specific peer result addresses these particular claims.

OpenEval supports claim C58 contextualizing the phenotype severity with citations to published work on other mutants. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses this contextual claim.

OpenEval supports claims C61-C62 establishing genetic context with citations to published work on Setx phenotypes. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses these background claims.

OpenEval supports claims C63-C65 comparing Topbp1B5/B5 to Setx null phenotypes, concluding the mutation has a more limited defect. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses this comparative analysis.
OpenEval supports claims C66-C68 regarding R-loop regulation model with citations and experimental observations. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses this mechanistic model.

OpenEval supports claims C70-C71 providing context for interpreting MLH1/MLH3 imbalance with citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses these contextual claims.
